sourceObjectiveEnglish: Direct object pronouns: Lo, la, los and las replace a direct object and agree with it: el libro → lo; las llaves → las.
sourceSpeakingEnglish: Role-play Preparar la mochila with a patient classmate. Practice direct object pronouns. Use this lesson's grammar, ask a related question, answer the partner, and confirm understanding. Keep language at beginner level; explain unfamiliar words in English when asked.

cards.proposalNote: Le is also a direct-object pronoun: it / him (je le trouve).
La can be a feminine article, a feminine direct-object pronoun, or “her” as an object; identify its role from context.
J’ai besoin de means “I need”; the French construction includes de.
Les is a plural article or direct-object pronoun for any gender; it can mean “them” in this lesson.

candidateGrammar.explanation: French direct-object pronouns replace a person or thing receiving the action: le livre → je le trouve; la clé → je la trouve; le sac à dos → je l’ouvre; les cahiers → je les range. Put the pronoun before the conjugated verb. Le and la both become l’ before a vowel or mute h, so l’ does not show gender: je l’ouvre, elle l’utilise. Les works for plural objects of any gender. The article comes before a noun (le livre); the object pronoun replaces the article and noun together (je le trouve).

model.book: Je cherche le livre et je le trouve.
model.backpack: J’ai le sac à dos et je l’ouvre.
model.notebooks: J’achète les cahiers et je les range.
model.keys: J’ai besoin des clés, mais je ne les vois pas.

candidateGrammar.caution: Les is plural for both masculine and feminine nouns. Avoir besoin de + les clés → j’ai besoin des clés (de + les = des); then les replaces les clés as the direct object of vois. In “Tu l’as, toi ?”, l’ could stand for le or la; context tells you which.

candidateSpeaking.text: Pack a school bag with a patient classmate. Ask about the book, backpack, notebooks, keys and pencil, and answer your partner’s questions. Name each object once, then replace it with le, la, l’ or les. Confirm whether your partner has the missing item. Keep language at beginner level; explain unfamiliar words in English when asked.

card8.reason: Spanish los marks masculine plural. French les covers masculine and feminine plural. The Spanish source gloss cannot be scored as an exclusive French gloss.

reader6.reason: The feminine Spanish direct object has an unstated referent. French l’ does not reveal gender. A contextual teaching choice is required.
